about: Hand-labelled statements about the photosynthesis page (eval/photosynthesis_card.json), each said by the classmate as 'Oh I see! So <statement>'. 'false' statements are contradicted by the page and must be flagged; 'true' ones are stated on the page and must pass. Labelled by the recipe author; review before relying on them.
true: plants make their own food in their leaves.
chlorophyll is a green pigment that traps energy from sunlight.
a plant needs sunlight, water and carbon dioxide to make food.
carbon dioxide gets into the leaf through tiny pores called stomata.
the roots absorb water from the soil.
oxygen is released into the air when the leaf makes food.
some of the glucose is stored as starch.
glucose is a kind of sugar.
water travels up the stem to the leaves.
the soil gives the plant water and minerals.
false: plants take their food from the soil.
carbon dioxide enters the plant through the roots.
photosynthesis happens mainly in the roots.
plants release carbon dioxide into the air as a by-product.
the leaf uses oxygen and water to make glucose.
plants need only water to make their food.
all the glucose is used straight away and none is stored.
animals make their own food the way plants do.
the food is made in the soil and then sent to the leaves.
held_out_note: Written after the v1 run, when the quantity-word fix was made, to check that the fix generalises. Not used while fixing.
held_out_true: a plant needs three things to make its food.
the glucose that is not used for energy is stored as starch.
photosynthesis happens mainly in the leaves.
held_out_false: a plant needs only sunlight to make its food.
plants never use any of their glucose for energy.
the leaf keeps all the oxygen it makes inside itself.
every part of the plant makes food equally.
